newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem "stronger than ever" despite strike.
newsitem.headline: Menem "stronger than ever" despite strike.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem is feeling stronger than ever despite a 36-hour general strike, growing social malaise and disastrous opinion poll results, two of his top aides said on Friday.

The Peronist leader phoned Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez and press chief Raul Delgado during a meeting with a handful of foreign correspondents to relay the message: "Tell them I'm stronger than ever."

Menem, reelected in May 1995 with 50 percent of the vote but now scoring under 20 percent in opinion polls, dismissed Thursday's mass rally and the strike ending at midnight on Friday as "a complete failure" and a "tourism" strike that was just an excuse for a long weekend.

Unions and opposition parties massed thousands of people -- they say 100,000, Menem police estimated 40,000 -- in the Plaza de Mayo outside the presidential palace to protest at a drive for fiscal austerity and more flexible labour laws.

The walkout, which unions estimate had 90 percent success, followed a 24-hour general strike in August and a "blackout" protest earlier this month, as well as a general strike last November. The main complaint of the main CGT labour federation, once Menem's ally, is high unemployment of 17.1 percent.
But the 66-year-old president is shrugging off the protest and forging ahead with labour reforms he says will help create jobs by making it easier for employers to take on staff.

"Let there be no doubt about the president's physical strength and health and his determination and will," said Rodriguez, dismissing social protest as "a series of blackouts that will cause a short-circuit" among the opposition.
Press chief Delgado denied Menem's intent was to sweep aside the unions. "But Menem has a clear idea of what he has to do and there is nothing that can get in his way," he said.

CGT Secretary General Rodolfo Daer, in his speech to the crowds, evoked party founder Juan Peron and accused Menem's government of "betraying" those like himself who voted for Menem last year and of "turning their back on the people."

But Menem, in a newspaper interview published on Friday, said "Peron suffered strikes as well" and his cabinet chief argued that Menem's policies are "pure Peronism -- the Peronist dream of turning this into a great country."
